cases.question: Why does my XIRR show '--'?
cases.answer: XIRR is a yearly return rate that accounts for when each instalment went in. With 7 months of instalments, a yearly rate isn't meaningful yet, which is why apps often leave it blank under a year. Your plain return so far is -4.8% (-₹1,675 on ₹35,000 invested).

The choice is yours: you can skip this instalment, pause until a month you pick, lower the amount, or stop the SIP altogether.

cases.question: Can I customize this debit amount dynamically based on my real-time bank balance?
cases.answer: Here's what each option does. Continue: the next instalment goes in as usual. Skip once: only the next instalment is skipped and the SIP carries on after. Pause: no instalments until the restart month you pick. Lower the amount: future instalments are smaller. Stop: no more instalments. In every case the ₹35,000 you've already invested stays invested and keeps moving with the market until you choose to redeem it. A debit that changes automatically with your bank balance isn't something I can set up.

cases.question: Why exactly did this transaction fail when there is more than enough cash sitting in the linked account?
cases.answer: I can't see your bank or mandate records, so I can't tell why that debit failed. Common reasons are a mandate limit lower than the instalment, a mandate that isn't fully set up, or a processing error at the bank. A failed instalment doesn't touch the units you already hold. Your app's support can check the exact reason, and your bank can confirm whether any charge was applied.
